To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the network capacity of a synchronous CDMA system with random spreading in a Rayleigh fading channel can be uniquely expressed as the product of the number of users and the effective target SIR, where the effective target S.I.R is the ratio between the target SIR and the effective bandwidth.
the network capacity of CDMA systems with random power control is characterized by the users’ QoS requirements and distributions of received powers.

the network capacity of a CDMA system with linear receivers is determined by the users' target SIR, the users' effective bandwidth and the distribution of the users' received powers, and that the network capacity is maximized when the users' received power distribution is uniform.

the fundamental problem of network capacity of CDMA systems with random power control and linear receivers, and provides a complete solution for this problem.
the network capacity and power allocation in CDMA systems with random power control in fading channels.
the fundamental issues of CDMA systems, and provides a comprehensive and unified treatment of the network capacity of CDMA systems in both single-class and multiple-class scenarios
